about.title: Personal Injury Help in Half Moon Bay, California
about.longDescription: Half Moon Bay's roads carry a steady mix of coastal commuters, farm traffic, and weekend visitors headed to the beaches, and that mix shows up in the numbers. In the most recent full year on record, the city logged 32 injury collisions and 45 people hurt, with no traffic deaths reported. Public crash records point to Route 1, SR-1, N Cabrillo Highway, and San Mateo Road as the corridors where collisions are most often reported, and Sunday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. see a noticeable cluster of reports — likely tied to weekend traffic heading back out of town. If you were hurt in a crash or another kind of accident here, we can help. Our team handles personal injury claims throughout the San Mateo County area, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Getting the right information quickly matters, especially with California's filing deadlines.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: A Filing Clock That Doesn't Wait
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Shut the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault. This applies whether the accident happened on SR-1 or in a parking lot.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California doesn't cap non-economic damages — like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life — in ordinary injury cases. That matters when an injury changes how you live day to day.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning our fee comes out of any settlement or award — not your pocket up front. If there's no recovery, there's no attorney fee.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Half Moon Bay?
items.answer: In California, you generally have two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your claim involves a government agency — like a road maintained by a city or county — that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some of the blame. Your total recovery is simply reduced by the percentage of fault assigned to you, not eliminated.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Half Moon Bay?
items.answer: Public crash records show that Route 1, SR-1, N Cabrillo Highway, and San Mateo Road are among the corridors with the highest reported collision counts in the city. Reports also tend to peak on Sunday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. These are neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No — California does not cap non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in typical personal injury cases. This is different from some other states and can matter significantly for injuries that affect your daily life long-term.

items.question: Does it cost anything to contact us?
items.answer: No. We offer free case reviews and work on contingency, so we only get paid if you recover compensation.
